title: Dynamics of Erased Distinctions
summary: A living synthesis of the project’s current view of coarse-graining: closure tracks which distinctions remain causally relevant, how erased distinctions return to visibility, and when representation repair must restore them.
thesis: Groovy Commutator studies the dynamics of distinctions erased by a representation.

title: Dimensional Closure and the Commutator Lift
summary: The lift is now a theorem: every binary finite-memory CA on Z^d has an exact, locally recoverable, self-synchronizing lift through every finite depth (proof by GPT-5.6 Sol, finite verification by Fable). It is beam-only and not unique; native G stays completion-dependent, with an exact tangent-versus-point explanation. Open here: the typed Groovy bundle. The Class-IV question moves to its own Program. The full-input first-floor forced tables of all 256 rules are cached and section 37 verified; cohabitation is nearly universal and its conflict metric does not predict pair regimes beyond the truth table.
thesis: When two dynamical paths fail to commute, represent the disagreement as a new coordinate and ask whether the enlarged representation closes.

title: Invariants Across Representation Contracts
summary: Eleven audits complete across four transformation types: global relabelings, an injective local recoding, linear and non-linear observations, and a change of wiring. Reflection and coprime whole-contract dilation preserve every exact property audited, with the seeded sweep labels only stable; complement conjugation and dilation are exactly covariant only when the companion object, the derivative or the observation, is transported with the rule; closure under an observation and its history cost are properties of the pair and are genuinely changed. A twelfth audit, factor locality on observation images, is accepted: idempotent observations bound the factor radius by construction, and the one whole-ring factor coincides with the one ring-dependent closure. A thirteenth audit certifies closure at every ring size from a sixteen-vertex pair graph: six audited observations stabilize from ring 7, and the two linear observations that alternate are certified to alternate forever. A fourteenth audit certifies refinement depth at most one at every ring from a 256-vertex pair graph per rule and finds that, unlike closure, depth on the full shift is not decided by the periodic configurations under four observations. The fifteenth audit decides full-shift depth at most two for every rule by sparse reachability, finds the same gap at depth two under seven observations, and shows that twenty-four rules with depth at most one on every ring have depth at least three on the full shift. The sixteenth audit takes the sparse method to depth three under the four non-linear observations, finds that twenty of those twenty-four rules have full-shift depth at least four, and tabulates every rule's full-shift depth class against its ring class: the two ladders agree only at closure. The Program page carries the verdict matrix and what each other program can use.
thesis: Which properties of a represented dynamics survive a declared change of representation contract, after transporting what must be transported, and at what cost?

title: Class-IV Refinement: what a lift makes visible
summary: Opened from the GPT handoff after the lift theorem closed the existence question. Inherits the Jev scout, the prospectively validated 54/110 discriminator (partial provenance), the cross-dimensional panel and the exact strip restriction. Its question is which distinctions become expressible and which observables transport when representation freedom is added, and whether a source rule confers a susceptibility to the persistence × spreading regime on its refinement fiber. First unit, the height-one fiber census, finds fiber(54) enriched (both-positive 0.47 against 0.37, 0.25, 0.22, 0.07 for 22, 0, 90, 204) with HighLife and Life typical of their fibers; the fixed-bit activity control is next. Jev Run 3 reproduces J1/J3/J5 under operational definitions alone. The 64-fiber census finds the phenotype non-additive in the six exposed bits on the spreading axis (birth-survival interactions), additive on the persistence axis; affine bases are not special. The handed census extends the restriction to an anisotropic family that is onto all 256 ECAs, so rule 110 finally has a fiber: it is both-positive at 0.543, tied at the top with its mirror 124 and with 54 and far above 30, with the enrichment on the persistence axis rather than spreading. A base's own 1D phenotype predicts its fiber's on both axes across all 256 bases; chirality is not detectable.
thesis: Treat Class IV as a phenotype under a declared observation contract and ask how it distributes over exact refinement families of a source rule, never as a label to reproduce.
